name: Langtang Valley Trek
notes: The page lists itineraries from 4 to 9 days. It states no highest point for the whole trek (Kyanjin Ri at 4300 m appears in a side trip).
sourceName: Himalayan Masters Adventure and Travel Company (agency guide - not an official figure)

name: Mardi Himal Trek
notes: The guide says the trek usually takes 4 to 7 trekking days and a 5-day plan is most common. It gives two high points, about 4200 m at the Upper Viewpoint and about 4500 m at Mardi Himal Base Camp (reached by only some trekkers), so none is recorded. Treks start from Dhampus, Kande or Phedi and finish at Siding or Lwang, then a drive to Pokhara.
sourceName: Nepal Hiking Team (agency guide - not an official figure)

name: Manang Trek
notes: Pokhara Info lists the trek as typically 7 to 9 days but describes it inconsistently (Manang to Muktinath via Thorong La in one place, a Pokhara to Pokhara itinerary in another), so no start, end or highest point is recorded. Thorong La (5416 m) and Tilicho Lake (4919 m) appear as nearby high points.
sourceName: Pokhara Info (local guide site - not an official figure)

name: Everest Base Camp Trek
notes: The guide says the classic trek takes 12 days from Kathmandu including flights and two acclimatisation days, and mentions a 14-day package. Highest destination is Everest Base Camp at 5364 m; Kala Patthar (about 5545 m) is an optional viewpoint. Flights to and from Lukla may use Kathmandu or Manthali (Ramechhap).
sourceName: Himalayan Recreation Treks & Expedition (agency guide - not an official figure)
